NEre talke to me, Ile make a star-cham ber matter of it. The Councell shall know it. Tho he be a knight, he shall not thinke to carrie it so away. M. Page I will not be wronged. For you Syr, I loue you, and for my cousen He comes to looke vpon your daughter. Sir Iohn, sir Iohn, you haue hurt my keeper, Kild my dogs, stolne my deere. Well this shall be answered. Well, the Councell shall know it. At hand mine host, at hand. M. Ford god den to you. God den an twentie good M. Page. I tell you sir we haue sport in hand. Harke you sir, Ile tell you what the sport shall be, Doctor Cayus and sir Hu are to fight, My merrie Host hath had the measuring Of their weapons, and hath Appointed them contrary places. Harke in your eare: I tell you what M. Page, I beleeue The Doctor is no Iester, heele laie it on: For tho we be Iustices and Doctors, And Church men, yet we are The sonnes of women M. Page: Ha with you mine host. How do you M. Doctor? He hath showne himselfe the wiser man M. Doctor: Sir Hugh is a Parson, and you a Phisition. You must Goe with me M. Doctor. We wil do it my host. Farwel M. Doctor. God saue you M. parson. Keep them asunder, take away their weapons. Let them keep their limbs hole, and hack our English. Afore God a mad host, come let vs goe. Mary I thanke you for that: To her cousin, to her. Fie cusse fie, thou art not right, O thou hadst a father. He will make you ioynter of three hun dred pound a yeare, he shall make you a Gentle woman. God saue you sir Iohn Falstaffe.
Nay good maister Shallow be perswaded by mee.
Nay surely my vncle shall not put it vp so. I haue matter in my head against you and your cogging companions, Pistoll and Nym. They carried mee to the Tauerne and made mee drunke, and afterward picked my pocket. I by this handkercher did he. Two faire shouell boord shillings, besides seuen groats in mill sixpences. By this light it was he then. Nay for my owne part, I would litle or no thing with you. I loue you well, and my vncle can tell you how my liuing stands. And if you can loue me why so. If not, why then happie man be his dole. Why by God, there's neuer a man in chri stendome can desire more. What haue you Beares in your Towne mistresse Anne, your dogs barke so? Ha how say you? I warrant your afeard of a Beare let loose, are you not? Now that's meate and drinke to me, Ile run yon to a Beare, and take her by the mussell, You neuer saw the like. But indeed I cannot blame you, For they are maruellous rough things. No faith not I. I thanke you, I cannot abide the smell of hot meate Nere since I broke my shin. Ile tel you how it came By my troth. A Fencer and I plaid three venies For a dish of stewd prunes, and I with my ward Defending my head, he hot my shin. Yes faith. I can eate no meate, I thanke you. Ile follow you sir, pray leade the way. Nay be God misteris Anne, you shall goe first, I haue more manners then so, I hope. Father Page I hope I haue your consent For Misteris Anne? I faith I know not what to say. Godeso theres a Iest indeed: why misteris An, I neuer made wil yet: I tha ̄ k God I am wise inough for that. I had a father misteris Anne, good vncle Tell the Iest how my father stole the goose out of The henloft. All this is nought, harke you mistresse Anne. Bride, by Gods lyd I thinke theres neuer a man in the worell hath that crosse fortune that I haue: begod I could cry for verie anger. Sonne, nay by God I am none of your son. Why so God saue me, tis a boy that I haue married. No neither, for I came to her in red as you bad me, and I cried mum, and hee cried budget, so well as euer you heard, and I haue married him.
Wil you not heare reasons M. Slenders? You should heare reasons. I pray you M. Shallowes let it be so. The matter is pud to arbitarments. The first man is M. Page, videlicet M. Page. The second is my selfe, videlicet my selfe. And the third and last man, is mine host of the gartyr. Here is sir Iohn himselfe now, looke you. Good vrdes sir Iohn, good vrdes. Hark you Simple, pray you beare this letter to Doctor Cayus house, the French Doctor. He is twell vp along the street, and enquire of his house for one mistris Quickly, his woman, or his try nurse, and deliuer this Letter to her, it tis about Maister Slender. Looke you, will you do it now? Pray you do, I must not be absent at the grace. I will goe make an end of my dinner, There is pepions and cheese behinde. I pray you do so much as see if you can espie Doctor Cayus comming, and giue me intelligence, Or bring me vrde if you please now. Ieshu ples mee, how my hart trobes, and trobes, And then she made him bedes of Roses, And a thousand fragrant poses, To shallow riueres. Now so kad vdge me, my hart Swelles more and more. Mee thinkes I can cry Verie well. There dwelt a man in Babylon, To shallow riuers and to falles, Melodious birds sing Madrigalles. Then it is verie necessary I put vp my sword, Pray giue me my cowne too, marke you. God plesse you all from his mercies sake now. There is reasons and causes in all things, I warrant you now. What is I pray you? I pray you who is it? Let vs know that. I had as leeue you should tel me of a messe of poredge, He is an arant lowsie beggerly knaue: And he is a coward beside. Harke you, let vs not be laughing stockes to other mens humors. By Ieshu I will knock your vrinalls about your knaues cockcomes, for missing your meetings and appointments. So kad vdge me, this is the pointment place, Witnes by my Host of the garter. Giue me your hand Doctor Cayus, We be all friends: But for mine hosts foolish knauery, let me alone. By Ieshu these are iealosies & distemperes. By so kad vdge me, tis verie necessarie He were put in pethlem. By Ieshu I verily thinke she is a witch indeed, I espied vnder her muster a great beard. Where is mine Host of the gartyr? Now my Host, I would desire you looke you now, To haue a care of your entertainments, For there is three sorts of cosen garmombles, Is cosen all the Host of Maidenhead & Readings, Now you are an honest man, and a scuruy beg gerly lowsie knaue beside: And can point wrong places, I tell you for good will, grate why mine Host. Come hither Peane, go to the countrie houses, And when you finde a slut that lies a sleepe, And all her dishes foule, and roome vnswept, With your long nailes pinch her till she crie, And sweare to mend her sluttish huswiferie. See I haue spied one by good luck, His bodie man, his head a buck. It is right indeed, he is full of lecheries and iniquitie. God plesse you sir Iohn, God plesse you. I trust me boyes Sir Iohn: and I was Also a Fairie that did helpe to pinch you. Butter is better then cheese sir Iohn, You are all butter, butter. Ieshu M. Slender, cannot you see but marrie boyes? I wil also dance & eat plums at your weddings.
And heres my hand, and if my daughter Like him so well as I, wee'l quickly haue it a match: In the meane time let me intreat you to soiourne Here a while. And on my life Ile vndertake To make you friends. No more now, I thinke it be almost dinner time, For my wife is come to meet vs. With all my hart, come along Gentlemen. Come, come Maister Slender, dinner staies for you. You shall not choose I say. The humor of it, quoth you: Heres a fellow frites humor out of his wits. How now man? How do you mistris Ford? Yes M. Ford, what of that sir? No by my troth do I not, I rather take them to be paltry lying knaues, Such as rather speakes of enuie, Then of any certaine they haue Of any thing. And for the knight, perhaps He hath spoke merrily, as the fashion of fat men Are: But should he loue my wife, I faith Ide turne her loose to him: And what he got more of her, Then ill lookes, and shrowd words, Why let me beare the penaltie of it. Here comes my ramping host of the garter, Ther's either licker in his hed, or mony in his purse, That he lookes so merily. Now mine Host? Maister Shallow you your selfe Haue bene a great fighter, Tho now a man of peace: Come M. Ford, shall we to dinner? I know these fellowes sticks in your minde. With all my hart sir, Ile follow you. God saue you M. Doctor Cayus. Sir Hugh is there, is hee? God saue you Sir Hugh. What the word and the sword, doth that a gree well? Well Sir Hugh, we are come to craue Your helpe and furtherance in a matter. I faith tis this sir Hugh. There is an anncient friend of ours, a man of verie good sort, so at oddes with one patience, that I am sure you would hartily grieue to see him. Now Sir Hugh, you are a scholler well red, and verie perswasiue, we would intreate you to see if you could intreat him to patience. I am shure you know him, tis Doctor Cayus. Why Ile laie my life tis the man That he should fight withall. I thanke you good M. Ford. I thank you sir, she is very well at home. You haue sonne Slender, but my wife here, Is altogether for maister Doctor. My host not with my co ̄ sent: the gentleman is Wilde, he knowes too much: If he take her, Let him take her simply: for my goods goes With my liking, and my liking goes not that way. Fie M. Ford you are too blame: M. Fenton I pray what make you here? You know my answere sir, shees not for you: Knowing my vow, to blame to vse me thus. Pray sir get you gon: Come hither daughter, Sonne Slender let me speak with you. Come wife, you an I will in, weele leaue M. Sle ̄ der And my daughter to talke together. M. Shallow, You may stay sir if you please. Fie M. Ford you are not to go abroad if you be in these fits. Come weele go for his minds sake. I misteris Ford, Falstaffe hath all the griefe, And in this knauerie my wife was the chiefe. I do not thinke heele come being so much deceiued. There must be some plot laide, or heele not come. Tis excellent, and my daughter Anne, Shall like a litle Fayrie be disguised. That will I do, and in a robe of white Ile cloath my daughter, and aduertise Slender To know her by that signe, and steale her thence, And vnknowne to my wife, shall marrie her. Well lets about this stratagem, I long To see deceit deceiued, and wrong haue wrong. Why how now sir Iohn, what a pair of horns in your hand? Nay be not angry wife, Ile tell thee true, It was my plot to deceiue thee so: And by this time your daughter's married To M. Slender, and see where he comes. Now sonne Slender, Where's your bride? Why whats the matter sonne Slender? No, why so? How a boy? why did you mistake the word? O I am vext at hart, what shal I do? At Church, what haue you done there? I cannot tel, and yet my hart's well eased, And yet it doth me good the Doctor missed. Come hither Fenton, and come hither daughter, Go too you might haue stai'd for my good will, But since your choise is made of one you loue, Here take her Fenton, & both happie proue.
Now M. Shallow, youle complaine of me to the Councell, I heare? But not kissed your keepers daughter. Ile answere it strait. I haue done all this. This is now answred. Twere better for you twere knowne in counsell, Youle be laught at. Good vrdes, good Cabidge. Slender I brake your head, What matter haue you against mee? What say you to this Pistoll, did you picke Maister Slenders purse Pistoll? What say you to this Pistoll? You heare these matters denide gentleme ̄ , You heare it. Mistresse Foord, I thinke your name is, If I mistake not. I shall desire your more aequaintance. The like of you good misteris Page. Mine Host of the Garter. Mine Host, I must turne away some of my followers. I sit at ten pound a weeke. Do good mine Host. Do Bardolfe, a Tapster is a good trade, An old cloake will make a new Ierkin, A withered seruingman, a fresh Tapster: Follow him Bardolfe. Well my Laddes, I am almost out at the heeles. Well I am glad I am so rid of this tinder Boy. His stealth was too open, his filching was like An vnskilfull singer, he kept not time. Well, afore God, I must cheat, I must cony catch. Which of you knowes Foord of this Towne? Well my honest Lads, Ile tell you what I am about. No gibes now Pistoll: indeed I am two yards In the wast, but now I am about no wast: Briefly, I am about thrift you rogues you, I do intend to make loue to Foords wife, I espie entertainment in her. She carues, she Discourses. She giues the lyre of inuitation, And euery part to be constured rightly is, I am Syr Iohn Falstaffes. Now the report goes, she hath all the rule Of her husbands purse. She hath legians of angels. Heree's a Letter to her. Heeres another to misteris Page. Who euen now gaue me good eies too, examined my exteriors with such a greedy intentio ̄ , with the beames of her beautie, that it seemed as she would a scorged me vp like a burning glasse. Here is ano ther Letter to her, shee beares the purse too. They shall be Excheckers to me, and Ile be cheaters to them both. They shall be my East and West Indies, and Ile trade to them both. Heere beare thou this Letter to mistresse Foord. And thou this to mistresse Page. Weele thriue Lads, we will thriue. Here sirrha beare me these Letters titely, Saile like my pinnice to the golden shores: Hence slaues, avant. Vanish like hailstones, goe. Falstaffe will learne the humor of this age, French thrift you rogue, my selfe and scirted Page. Ile not lend thee a peny. Not a pennie: I haue beene content you shuld lay my countenance to pawne: I haue grated vpon my good friends for 3. repriues, for you and your Coach-fellow Nym, else you might a looked thorow a grate like a geminy of babones. I am dam ned in hell for swearing to Gentlemen your good souldiers and tall fellowes: And when mistrisse Bri get lost the handle of her Fan, I tooked on my ho thou hadst it not. Reason you rogue, reason. Doest thou thinke Ile indanger my soule gratis? In briefe, hang no more about mee, I am no gybit for you. A short knife and a throng to your manner of pickt hatch, goe. Youle not beare a Letter for me you rogue you: you stand vpon your honor. Why thou vnconfinable basenesse thou, tis as much as I can do to keep the termes of my honor precise. I, I my selfe sometimes, leauing the feare of God on the left hand, am faine to shuffel, to filch & to lurch. And yet you stand vpon your honor, you rogue. You, you. Well, gotoo, away, no more. Good den faire wife. Faire mayd then. Say on I prethy, heeres none but my owne houshold. So from Mistresse Foord. Goeon. Well, come Misteris Ford, Misteris Ford. Nay prethy be briefe my good she Mercury. So betweene eight and nine: Well commend me to thy mistris, tel her I will not faile her: Boy giue her my purse. From misteris Page? I prethy what of her? Not I, I assure thee: setting the atraction of my Good parts aside, I vse no other inchantments: But harke thee, hath misteris Page & mistris Ford, Acquainted each other how dearly they loue me? Well farwel, commend me to misteris Ford, I will not faile her say. M. Brooke, hees welcome: Bid him come vp, Such Brookes are alwaies welcome to me: A Iack, will thy old bodie yet hold out? Wilt thou after the expence of so much mony Be now a gainer? Good bodie I thanke thee, And Ile make more of thee then I ha done: Ha, ha, misteris Ford, and misteris Page, haue I caught you a the hip? go too. And you too, would you speak with me? Mary would I sir, I am somewhat bolde to trouble you, My name is Brooke. Good M. Brooke your verie welcome. Mony is a good souldier sir, and will on. O Lord, would I could tell how to deserue To be your porter. Verie well sir, proceed. O good sir. Haue you importuned her by any means? Of what qualitie is your loue then? And to what end haue you vnfolded this to me? Why would it apply well to the veruensie of your affection, That another should possesse what you would enioy? Meethinks you prescribe verie proposterously To your selfe. Well M. Brooke, Ile first make bold with your mony, Next, giue me your hand. Lastly, you shall And you will, enioy Fords wife. M. Brooke, I say you shall. Want no Misteris Ford M. Brooke, You shall want none. Euen as you came to me, Her spokes mate, her go between parted from me: I may tell you M. Brooke, I am to meet her Between 8. and 9. for at that time the Iealous Cuckally knaue her husband wil be from home, Come to me soone at night, you shall know how I speed M. Brooke. Hang him poore cuckally knaue, I know him not, And yet I wrong him to call him poore. For they Say the cuckally knaue hath legions of angels, For the which his wife seemes to me well fauored, And Ile vse her as the key of the cuckally knaues Coffer, and there's my randeuowes. Hang him cuckally knaue, Ile stare him Out of his wits, Ile keepe him in awe With this my cudgell: It shall hang like a meator Ore the wittolly knaues head, M. Brooke thou shalt See I will predominate ore the peasant, And thou shalt lie with his wife. M. Brooke Thou shalt know him for knaue and cuckold, Come to me soone at night. Haue I caught my heauenlie Iewel? Why now let me die. I haue liued long inough, This is the happie houre I haue desired to see, Now shall I sin in my wish, I would thy husband were dead. By the Lord, Ide make thee my Ladie. Goe too, I see how thy eie doth emulate the Diamond. And how the arched bent of thy brow Would become the ship tire, the tire vellet, Oranie Venetian attire, I see it. By the Lord thou art a traitor to saie so: What made me loue thee? Let that perswade thee Ther's somewhat extraordinarie in thee: Goe too I loue thee: Mistris Ford, I cannot cog, I cannot prate, like one Of these fellowes that smels like Bucklers-berie, In simple time, but I loue thee, And none but thee. I thou mightest as well saie I loue to walke by the Counter gate, VVhich is as hatefull to me As the reake of a lime kill. Let me see, let me see, Ile in, Ile in, Follow your friends counsell. I loue thee, and none but thee: Helpe me to conuey me hence, Ile neuer come here more. Bid her come vp. Let me put some Sacke among this cold water, for my belly is as cold as if I had swallowed snow-balles for pilles. Now whats the newes with you? Misteris Ford, I haue had Ford inough, I haue bene throwne into the Ford, my belly is full Of Ford: she hath tickled mee. Ten, and eleuen, saiest thou? Well, tell her Ile meet her. Let her but think Of mans frailtie: Let her iudge what man is, And then thinke of me. And so farwell. I will not faile. Commend me to her. I wonder I heare not of M. Brooke, I like his Mony well. By the masse here he is. Welcome good M. Brooke. You come to know how matters goes. M. Brooke I will not lie to you sir, I was there at my appointed time. Verie il fauouredly sir. No M. Brooke, but you shall heare. After we had kissed and imbraced, and as it were euen amid the prologue of our incounter, who should come, but the iealous knaue her husband, and a rabble of his companions at his heeles, thither prouoked and instigated by his distemper. And what to do thinke you? to search for his wiues loue. Euen so, plainly so. Whilst I was there. You shall heare sir, as God would haue it, A litle before comes me one Pages wife, Giues her intelligence of her husbands Approach: and by her inuention, and Fords wiues Distraction, conueyd me into a buck-basket. By the Lord a buck-basket, rammed me in With foule shirts, stokins, greasie napkins, That M. Brooke, there was a compound of the most Villanous smel, that euer offended nostrill. Ile tell you M. Brooke, by the Lord for your sake I suffered three egregious deaths: First to be Crammed like a good bilbo, in the circomference Of a pack, Hilt to point, heele to head: and then to Be stewed in my owne grease like a Dutch dish: A man of my kidney; by the Lord it was maruell I Escaped suffication; and in the heat of all this, To be throwne into Thames like a horshoo hot: Maister Brooke, thinke of that hissing heate, Maister Brooke. M. Brooke, Ile be throwne into Etna As I haue bene in the Thames, Ere I thus leaue her: I haue receiued Another appointment of meeting, Between ten and eleuen is the houre. What are you sure of your husband now? No Ile come no more in the basket, Ile creep vp into the chimney. Why then Ile goe out of doores. For Gods sake deuise any extremitie, Rather then a mischiefe. Come for God sake, any thing. Now mine Host. Indeed mine host there was afat woman with me, But she is gone. Marry was it Musselshell, what would you? I talked with the woman about it. Marry she ses the very same man that Beguiled maister Slender of his chaine, Cousoned him of it. I tike, who more bolde. Marry was there mine host, one that taught Me more wit then I learned this 7. yeare, And I paid nothing for it, But was paid for my learning. Would all the worell were cosened for me, For I am cousoned and beaten too. Well, I neuer prospered since I forswore My selfe at Primero: and my winde Were but long inough to say my prayers, Ide repent, now from whence come you? The diuell take the one partie, And his dam the other, And theyle be both bestowed. I haue endured more for their sakes, Then man is able to endure. What tellest me of blacke and blew, I haue bene beaten all the colours in the Rainbow, And in my escape like to a bene apprehended For a witch of Brainford, and set in the stockes. Come goe with me into my chamber, Ile heare thee. This is the third time, well Ile venter, They say there is good luck in old numbers, Ioue transformed himselfe into a bull, And I am here a Stag, and I thinke the fattest In all Windsor forrest: well I stand here For Horne the hunter, waiting my Does comming. Art thou come my doe? what and thou too? Welcome Ladies. This makes amends for all. Come diuide me betweene you, each a hanch, For my horns Ile bequeath the ̄ to your husbands, Do I speake like Horne the hunter, ha? God blesse me from that wealch Fairie. God send me good fortune now, and I care not. Horne the hunter quoth you: am I a ghost? Sblood the Fairies hath made a ghost of me: What hunting at this time at night? Ile lay my life the mad Prince of Wales Is stealing his fathers Deare. How now who haue we here, what is all Windsor stirring? Are you there? Iest, tis well, haue I liued to these yeares To be gulled now, now to be ridden? Why then these were not Fairies? By the Lord I was twice or thrise in the mind They were not, and yet the grosnesse Of the fopperie perswaded me they were. Well, and the fine wits of the Court heare this, Thayle so whip me with their keene Iests, That thayle melt me out like tallow, Drop by drop out of my grease. Boyes! I, tis well I am your May-pole, You haue the start of mee, Am I ridden too with a wealch goate? With a peece of toasted cheese? It hath cost me well, I haue bene well pinched and washed. I am glad yet that your arrow hath glanced
Sir Iohn, and Maister mine, I combat craue Of this same laten bilbo. I do retort the lie Euen in thy gorge, thy gorge, thy gorge. Shall I sir Panderowes of Troy become? And by my sword were steele. Then Lucifer take all.
Syr my honor is not for many words, But if you run bace humors of me, I will say mary trap. And there's the humor of it. His minde is not heroick. And theres the humor of it. I thanke thee for that humor. The good humor is to steale at a minutes rest. Here take your humor Letter againe, For my part, I will keepe the hauior Of reputation. And theres the humor of it. I haue operations in my head, which are humors of reuenge. By Welkin and her Fairies. With both the humors I will disclose this loue to Page. Ile poses him with Iallowes, And theres the humor of it. Let vs about it then. Syr the humor of it is, he loues your wife, I should ha borne the humor Letter to her: I speake and I auouch tis true: My name is Nym. Farwell, I loue not the humor of bread and cheese: And theres the humor of it.
Your mistake sir is nothing but in the Mistresse. But my husbands name is Foord sir. In loue, now in the name of God with whom?
With all my hart sir Iohn. Come husband will you goe? Dinner staies for vs. Mistresse Page I loue you. Aske me no reason, Because theyr impossible to alledge. Your faire, And I am fat. You loue sack, so do I: As I am sure I haue no mind but to loue, So I know you haue no hart but to grant A souldier doth not vse many words, where a knowes A letter may serue for a sentence. I loue you, And so I leaue you. Now Ieshu blesse me, am I methomorphised? I thinke I knowe not my selfe. Why what a Gods name doth this man see in me, that thus he shootes at my honestie? Well but that I knowe my owne heart, I should scarcely perswade my selfe I were hand. Why what an vnreasonable woolsack is this. He was neuer twice in my companie, and if then I thought I gaue such assurance with my eies, Ide pul them out, they should neuer see more holie daies. Well, I shall trust fat men the worse while I liue for his sake. O God that I knew how to be reuenged of him. But in good time, heeres mistresse Foord. O woman I am I know not what: In loue vp to the hard eares. I was neuer in such a case in my life. With one that sweares he loues me, And I must not choose but do the like againe: I prethie looke on that Letter. Why this is right my letter. O most notorious villaine! Why what a bladder of iniquitie is this? Lets be reuenged what so ere we do. See where our husbands are, Mine's as far from Iealousie, As I am from wronging him. How now sweet hart, how dost thou? O sheele serue excellent. Now you come to see my daughter An I am sure. Come go in with me. Come Mis. Ford. Mistresse Ford, Mis. Ford, where are you? Why your husband woman is co ̄ ming, With halfe Windsor at his heeles, To looke for a gentleman that he ses Is hid in his house: his wifes sweet hart. Tis too true woman. Therefore if you Haue any here, away with him, or your vndone for euer. Gode body woman, do not stand what shal I do, and what shall I do. Better any shift, rather then you shamed. Looke heere, here's a buck-bas ket, if hee be a man of any reasonable sise, heele in here. Fie sir Iohn is this your loue? Go too. He is in a pittifull taking. Hang him dishonest slaue, we cannot vse Him bad inough. This is excellent for your Husbands iealousie. Nay we wil send to Falstaffe once again, Tis great pittie we should leaue him: What wiues may be merry, and yet honest too. Here comes your husband, stand aside. Did you heare that? I faith tis not well M. Ford to suspect Her thus without cause. I faith M. Fento ̄ tis as my husband please. For my part Ile neither hinder you, nor further you. Misteris Ford, why woman your husband is in his old vaine againe, hees comming to search for your sweet heart, but I am glad he is not here. Why then you'r vndone woman, vnles you make some meanes to shift him away. Alas I know not what meanes to make, If there were any womans apparell would fit him, He might put on a gowne and a mufler, And so escape. And she is altogether as fat as he. Come goe with me sir Iohn, Ile helpe to dresse you. O by no meanes, send to him againe. Let vs alone for that. Heare my deuice. Oft haue you heard since Horne the hunter dyed, That women to affright their litle children, Ses that he walkes in shape of a great stagge. Now for that Falstaffe hath bene so deceiued, As that he dares not venture to the house, Weele send him word to meet vs in the field, Disguised like Horne, with huge horns on his head, The houre shalbe iust betweene twelue and one, And at that time we will meet him both: Then would I haue you present there at hand, With litle boyes disguised and dressed like Fayries, For to affright fat Falstaffe in the woods. And then to make a period to the Iest, Tell Falstaffe all, I thinke this will do best. And in that Maske Ile make the Doctor steale my daughter An, & ere my husband knowes it, to carrie her to Church, and marrie her. Why then we are reuenged sufficiently. First he was carried and throwne in the Thames, Next beaten well, I am sure youle witnes that. Sir Iohn, where are you? God forgiue me, what noise is this? No sir Iohn but boyes. How a boy? Here comes the man that hath deceiued vs all: How now daughter, where haue you bin? Altho that I haue missed in my intent, Yet I am glad my husbands match was crossed, Here M. Fenton, take her, and God giue thee ioy.
Now forsooth why do you stay me? What would you with me?
You say well M. Slender. But first you must giue me leaue to Be acquainted with your humor, And afterward to loue you if I can. I cannot tell M. Slender, I thinke there be. Yes trust me. Will you goe in to dinner M. Slendor? The meate staies for you. Well sir, I will not be troublesome. Now M. Slender, whats your will? O God how many grosse faults are hid, And couered in three hundred pound a yeare? Well M. Slender, within a day or two Ile tell you more. At Curch forsooth.
I warrant you Sir. I indeed that is his name. Indeed my maisters beard is kane colored. I indeed is it. I by my faith you are a good staie to him. I be shrow me, one woman to do all this, Is very painfull. Is he indeed? O Lord sir no: I am no theefe, I am a Seruingman: My name is Iohn Simple, I brought a Letter sir From my M. Slender, about misteris Anne Page Sir: Indeed that is my comming. O God what a furious man is this? I sir, Ile tell him so. Mary will I, I am glad I am got hence. I will Sir. Sir here is M. Page, and M. Shallow, Comming hither as fast as they can. Sir, I am sent fro ̄ my M. to sir Iohn Falstaffe. Sir I should speak with an old woman that went vp into his chamber. Pray sir was it not the wise woman of Brain ford? Marry sir my maister Slender sent me to her, To know whether one Nim that hath his chaine, Cousoned him of it, or no. And I pray sir what ses she? May I be bolde to tell my maister so sir? I thanke you sir, I shall make my maister a glad man at these tydings, God be with you sir.
What ses my bully Rooke? Speake schollerly and wisely. Discard bully, Hercules cassire. Let them wag, trot, trot. Thou art an Emperour Caesar, Phesser and Kesar bully. Ile entertaine Bardolfe. He shall tap, he shall draw. Said I well, bully Hector? I haue spoke. Let him follow. Bardolfe Let me see thee froth, and lyme. I am at A word. Follow, follow. God blesse you my bully rookes, God blesse you. Cauelera Iustice I say. Tell him cauelira Iustice: tell him bully rooke. What ses my bully rooke? Here boyes, shall we wag, shall we wag? God blesse thee my bully doctor, God blesse thee, Bully to see thee fight, to see thee foine, to see thee trauerse, to see thee here, to see thee there, to see thee passe the punto. The stock, the reuerse, the distance: the montnce is a dead my francoyes? Is a dead my Ethiopian? Ha what ses my gallon? my escuolapis? Is a dead bullies taile, is a dead? Thou art a castallian king vrinall. Hector of Greece my boy. Pardon bully Iustice. A word monsire mockwater. That is in our English tongue, Vallorbully, vallor. He will claperclaw thee titely bully. That is, he will make thee amends. He is there: goe see what humor hee is in, Ile bring the Doctor about by the fields: Will it do well? Let him die, but first fheth your impatience, Throw cold water on your collor, com go with me Through the fields to Frogmore, and Ile bring thee Where mistris An Page is a feasting at a farm house, And thou shalt wear hir cried game: sed I wel bully For the which Ile be thy aduersary To misteris An Page: Sed I well? Let vs wag then. Disarme, let them question. Peace I say gawle and gawlia, French and Wealch, Soule curer, and bodie curer. Peace I say, heare mine host of the garter, Am I wise? am I polliticke? am I Matchauil? Shall I lose my doctor? No, he giues me the motio ̄ s And the potions. Shall I lose my parson, my sir Hu? No, he giues me the prouerbes, and •• e nouerbes: Giue me thy hand terestiall, So giue me thy hand celestiall: So boyes of art I haue deceiued you both, I haue directed you to wrong places, Your hearts are mightie, you skins are whole, Bardolfe laie their swords to pawne. Follow me lads Of peace, follow me. Ha, ra, la. Follow. But what say you to yong Maister Fenton? He capers, he daunces, he writes verses, he smelles All April and May: he wil cary it, he wil carit, Tis in his betmes he wil carite. The Duke, what Duke? let me speake with the Gentlemen, do they speake English? No Bardolfe, let them alone, Ile sauce them: They haue had my house a weeke at command, I haue turned away my other guesse, They shall haue my horses Bardolfe, They must come off, Ile sawce them. What would thou haue boore, what thick-skin? Speake, breath, discus, short, quick, briefe, snap. Sir Iohn, theres his Castle, his standing bed, his trundle bed, his chamber is painted about with the story of the prodigall, fresh and new, go knock, heele speak like an Antripophiginian to thee: Knock I say. An old woman, the knight may be robbed, Ile call bully knight, bully sir Iohn. Speake from thy Lungs military: it is thine host, thy Ephesian calls. Thou art clarkly sir Iohn, thou art clarkly, Was there a wise woman with thee? Why man, where be my horses? where be the Germanes? O here sir in perplexitie. I am cosened Hugh, and coy Bardolfe, Sweet knight assist me, I am cosened. Speake not to me sir, my mind is heauie, I haue had a great losse. Well sir Ile heare you, and at least keep your counsell. Now which means she to deceiue, father or mother? But how will you come to steale her from among the ̄ ? Well, husband your deuice, Ile to the Vicar, Bring you the maide, you shall not lacke a Priest.
I will sir, Ile warrant you Ile make a good shift to liue. Sir heer's a Gentleman, One M. Brooke, would speak with you, He hath sent you a cup of sacke. I sir, there's a woman below would speake with you. Syr heere be three Gentlemen come from the Duke the Stanger sir, would haue your horse. O Lord sir cousonage, plaine cousonage. Rid away with your horses: After I came beyond Maidenhead, They flung me in a slow of myre, & away they ran.
O bace gongarian wight, wilt thou the spic ket willd? Why then let cybes insue. Tis so indeed Nym, thou hast hit it right. I ken the wight, he is of substance good. Two yards and more. He hath studied her well, out of honestie Into English. As many diuels attend her. And to her boy say I. And art thou gone? Teaster Ile haue in pouch When thou shalt want, bace Phrygian Turke. Wilt thou reuenge? By wit, or sword? And I to Foord will likewise tell How Falstaffe varlot vilde, Would haue her loue, his doue would proue, And eke his bed defile. Ile second thee: sir Corporall Nym troope on. Ford the words I speake are forst: Beware, take heed, for Falstaffe loues thy wife: When Pistoll lies do this. He wooes both yong and old, both rich and poore None comes amis. I say he loues thy wife: Faire warning did I giue, take heed, For sommer comes, and Cuckoo birds appeare: Page belieue him what he ses. Away sir Corporall Nym. I will retort the sum in equipage. Didst thou not share? hadst thou not fif teene pence? I do recant: what woulst thou more of man?
M. Slender is your Masters name say you? How say you? I take it hee is somewhat a weakly man: And he has as it were a whay coloured beard. Kane colour, you say well. And is this Letter from sir Yon, about Misteris An, Is it not? So: and your Maister would haue me as it twere to speak to misteris Anne concerning him: I promise you my M. hath a great affectioned mind to mistresse Anne himselfe. And if he should know that I should as they say, giue my verdit for any one but himselfe, I should heare of it throughly: For I tell you friend, he puts all his priuities in me. Am I? I and you knew all yowd say so: Washing, brewing, baking, all goes through my hands, Or else it would be but a woe house. Are you auised of that? I, I warrant you, Take all, and paie all, all goe through my hands, And he is such a honest man, and he should chance To come home and finde a man here, we should Haue no who with him. He is a parlowes man. Is he quoth you? God keepe him abroad: Lord blesse me, who knocks there? For Gods sake step into the Counting house, While I goe see whose at doore. What Iohn Rugby, Iohn, Are you come home sir alreadie? Ieshu blesse me, we are all vndone. Nay it is well he is no worse: I am glad he is so quiet. VVell my friend, I cannot tarry, tell your Maister Ile doo what I can for him, And so farewell. I forsooth that is my comming. Good you god den sir. Not so ant like your worship. That I am Ile be sworne, as my mother was The first houre I was borne. Sir I would speake with you in priuate. Are they so? Now God blesse them, and make them his seruants. Syr I come from Mistresse Foord. I sir, she hath sent me to you to let you Vnderstand she hath receiued your Letter, And let me tell you, she is one stands vpon her credit. I sir, and as they say, she is not the first Hath bene led in a fooles paradice. Mary sir, sheed haue you meet her between eight and nine. I forsooth, for then her husband goes a birding, Nay sir I haue another arant to do to you From misteris Page: By my troth I think you work by Inchantments, Els they could neuer loue you as they doo: Well sir, she loues you extreemly: And let me tell you, shees one that feares God, And her husband giues her leaue to do all: For he is not halfe so iealousie as M. Ford is. O God no sir: there were a iest indeed. God be with your worship. I come from misteris Ford forsooth. O Lord sir, she is the sorrowfullest woman that her seruants mistooke, that euer liued. And sir, she would desire you of all loues you will meet her once againe, to morrow sir, betweene ten and ele uen, and she hopes to make amends for all. I forsooth. Speake to Misteris Page. How say you this was my doings? I bid you speake to misteris Page. By my troth so I will, good hart. M. Shallow, M. Page would pray you to come you, and you M. Slender, and you mistris An. Indeed I will, Ile speake what I can for you, But specially for M. Fenton: But specially of all for my Maister. And indeed I will do what I can for them all three. From the two parties forsooth. O Lord sir, they are the sorowfulst creatures That euer liued: specially mistresse Ford, Her husband hath beaten her that she is all Blacke and blew poore soule. Well sir, she is a sorrowfull woman, And I hope when you heare my errant, Youle be perswaded to the contrarie. Away begon, his mind fulfill, And looke that none of you stand still. Some do that thing, some do this, All do something, none amis. Looke euery one about this round, And if that any here be found, For his presumption in this place, Spare neither legge, arme, head, nor face. Go strait, and do as I commaund, And take a Taper in your hand, And set it to his fingers endes, And if you see it him offends, And that he starteth at the flame, Then is he mortall, know his name: If with an F. it doth begin, Why then be shure he is full of sin. About it then, and know the truth, Of this same metamorphised youth. A little distant from him stand, And euery one take hand in hand, And compasse him within a ring, First pinch him well, and after sing.

How now Mistris Page, are you reading Loue Letters? How do you woman? Ile match your letter iust with the like, Line for line, word for word. Only the name Of misteris Page, and misteris Foord disagrees: Do me the kindnes to looke vpon this. Reuenged, if we liue weel be reuenged. O Lord if my husband should see this Letter, I faith this would euen giue edge to his Iealousie. Well I thanke you good M. Page. How now husband, how chaunce thou art so me lancholy? God saue me, see who yonder is: Weele set her a worke in this businesse. I follow you Mistresse Page. Sirrha, if your M. aske you whither You carry this basket, say to the Launderers, I hope you know how to bestow it? Go get you in. Well sir Iohn, I beleeue I shall serue you such a trick, You shall haue little mind to come againe. Why how then sir Iohn? Alas sir Iohn, I should be a verie simple Ladie. A plaine kercher sir Iohn, would fit me better. Sir Iohn, I am afraid you loue misteris Page. O Lord step aside good sir Iohn. How now Misteris Page whats the matter? Speak louder. But I hope tis not true Misteris Page. Alas mistresse Page, what shall I do? Here is a gentleman my friend, how shall I do? Alas I feare he is too big. Now let it go, you had best meddle with buck-washing. I, I, peace. Do you heare? when your M. comes take vp this basket as you did before, and if your M. bid you set it downe, obey him. Syr Iohn welcome. He is gone a birding sir Iohn, and I hope will not come home yet. Gods body here is misteris Page, Step behind the arras good sir Iohn. O God misteris Page the knight is here, What shall I do? Alas I know no meanes, vnlesse we put him in the basket againe. There they vse to discharge their Fowling peeces. I that will serue him of my word. What is the reason that you vse me thus? I Gods my record do you. And if you mistrust me in any ill sort. But sweete heart shall wee leaue olde Falstaffe so? But who will buy the silkes to tyre the boyes?
Why sir my wife is not young. Melancholy, I am not melancholy. Goe get you in, goe. Mine Host a the garter: A word with you sir. No neuer Sir. I faith sir, like a faire house set vpon Another mans foundation. Want no mony Syr Iohn, you shall want none. Sir do you know Ford? Meethinkes sir it were very good that you knew Ford, that you might shun him. What a damned epicurian is this? My wife hath sent for him, the plot is laid: Page is an Asse, a foole. A secure Asse, Ile sooner trust an Irishman with my Aquauita bottle, Sir Hu our parson with my cheese, A theefe to walk my ambling gelding, the ̄ my wife With her selfe: then she plots, then she ruminates, And what she thinkes in her hart she may effect, Sheele breake her hart but she will effect it. God be praised, God be praised for my iealousie: Well Ile goe preuent him, the time drawes on, Better an houre too soone, then a minit too late, Gods my lise cuckold, cuckold. I may chance to make him drinke in pipe wine, First come gentlemen. Come pray along, you shall see all. How now who goes heare? whither goes this? Whither goes it? set it downe. Buck, good buck, pray come along, Maister Page take my keyes: helpe to search. Good Sir Hugh pray come along, helpe a little, a little, Ile shew you all. Thats my comming indeed sir Iohn. A buck basket! Well sir then my shute is void? Youle vndertake it no more? Well sed brazen face, hold it out, You youth in a basket, come out here, Pull out the cloathes, search. Pray come helpe me to search, pray now. Well wife, heere take my hand, vpon my soule I loue thee dearer then I do my life, and ioy I hnue so true and constant wife, my iealousie shall neuer more offend thee. Those hornes he ment to place vpon my head, And M. Brooke and he should be the men: Why how now sir Iohn, why are you thus amazed? We know the Fairies man that pinched you so, Your throwing in the Thames, your beating well, And whats to come sir Iohn, that can we tell. All parties pleased, now let vs in to feast, And laugh at Slender, and the Doctors ieast. He hath got the maiden, each of you a boy To waite vpon you, so God giue you ioy, And sir Iohn Falstaffe now shal you keep your word, For Brooke this night shall lye with mistris Ford.
M. Page did you heare what these fellowes said? Do you thinke it is true that they told vs? Nay I do not mistrust my wife, Yet Ide be loth to turne them together, A man may be too confident. None I protest: But tell him my name Is Brooke, onlie for a Iest. No in good sadnesse not in mine: Yet for all this Ile try it further, I will not leaue it so: Come M. Page, shall we to dinner? God saue you sir. I faith sir I am a gentleman and a traueller, That haue seen somewhat. And I haue often heard That if mony goes before, all waies lie open. I faith sir, and I haue a bag here, Would you wood helpe me to beare it. That may you easily sir Iohn: I haue an earnest Sute to you. But good sir Iohn when I haue Told you my griefe, cast one eie of your owne Estate, since your selfe knew what tis to be Such an offender. Sir I am deeply in loue with one Fords wife Of this Towne. Now sir Iohn you are a gentleman Of good discoursing, well beloued among Ladies, A man of such parts that might win 20. such as she. Nay beleeue it sir Iohn, for tis time. Now my loue Is so grounded vpon her, that without her loue I shall hardly liue. O sir, when I haue told you that, I told you all: For she sir stands so pure in the firme state Of her honestie, that she is too bright to be looked Against: Now could I come against her With some detectio ̄ , I should sooner perswade her From her marriage vow, and a hundred such nice Tearmes that sheele stand vpon. No sir, for by that meanes should I be cer taine of that which I now misdoubt. O good sir. The time drawes on he shuld come to my house, Well wife, you had best worke closely, Or I am like to goe beyond your cunning: I now wil seek my guesse that comes to dinner, And in good time see where they all are come. By my faith a knot well met: your welcome all. Welcome good M. Page, I would your daughter were here. Well I pray go home with me to dinner: Besides your cheare Ile shew you wonders: Ile Shew you a monster. You shall go with me. M. Page, and so shall you sir Hugh, and you Maister Doctor. I can find no body within, it may be he lied. Well Ile not let it go so, yet Ile trie further. Wel I pray bear with me, M. Page pardo ̄ me. I suffer for it, I suffer for it: God saue you sir. And how sped you sir? Why sir, did she change her determination? While ye were there? And did he search and could not find you? Is this a dreame? Is it a vision? Maister Ford, maister Ford, awake maister Ford, There is a hole made in your best coat M. Ford, And a man shall not only endure this wrong, But shall stand vnder the taunt of names, Lucifer is a good name, Barbason good: good Diuels names: But cuckold, wittold, godeso The diuel himselfe hath not such a name: And they may hang hats here, and napkins here Vpon my hornes: Well Ile home, I ferit him, And vnlesse the diuel himselfe should aide him, Ile search vnpossible places: Ile about it, Least I repent too late: Come along I pray, you shal know the cause, How now whither goe you? Ha whither go you? Set downe the basket you ssaue, You panderly rogue set it downe. Come hither set downe the basket, Misteris Ford the modest woman, Misteris Ford the vertuous woman, She that hath the iealous foole to her husband, I mistrust you without cause do I not? M. Page, as I am an honest man M. Page, There was one conueyd out of my house here ye sterday out of this basket, why may he not be here now? Old woman, what old woman? Let me alone, Ile to him once againe like Brooke, and know his mind whether heele come or not. There is a further matter yet sir Iohn, There's 20. pound you borrowed of M. Brooke Sir Iohn, And it must be paid to M. Ford Sir Iohn. Well here is my hand, all's forgiuen at last.

speeches.Pa:: True maister Shallow: Wel let it be so, and to morrow I inuite you all To my house to dinner: and in the morning weele A birding, I haue an excellent Hauke for the bush.

speeches.Ford:: Well I pray no more, another time Ile tell you all: The mean time go dine with me, pardo ̄ me wife, I am sorie. M. Page pray goe in to dinner, Another time Ile tell you all. Let it be so: Come M. Page, come wife: I pray you come in all, your welcome, pray come in. Why sir, tis almost ten alreadie: I faith M. Page neuer chafe your selfe, She hath made her choise wheras her hart was fixt, Then tis in vaine for you to storme or fret.
speeches.Fal:: Bardolfe brew me a pottle sack presently: Simply of it selfe, Ile none of these pullets sperme In my drinke: goe make haste. Haue I liued to be carried in a basket and throwne into the Thames like a barow of But chers offoll. Well, and I be serued such another tricke, Ile giue them leaue to take out my braines and butter them, and giue them to a dog for a new yeares gift. Sblood, the rogues slided me in with as little remorse as if they had gone to drowne a blind bitches puppies in the litter: and they might know by my sise I haue a kind of alacritie in sinking: and the bottom had bin as deep as hell I should downe. I had bene drowned, but that the shore was sheluie and somewhat shallowe: a death that I abhorre. For you know the water swelles a man: and what a thing should I haue bene whe ̄ I had bene swelled: By the Lord a mountaine of money. Now is the Sacke brewed? Is it? why then will I addresse my selfe For my appointment: M. Brooke come to me soone At night, and you shall know how I speed, And the end shall be, you shall enioy her loue: You shall cuckold Foord: Come to mee soone at at night.
speeches.Bar:: With Egges sir? Ile call them to you sir.
speeches.Fen:: Tell me sweet Nan, how doest thou yet resolue, Shall foolish Slender haue thee to his wife? Or one as wise as he, the learned Doctor? Shall such as they enioy thy maiden hart? Thou knowst that I haue alwaies loued thee deare, And thou hast oft times swore the like to me. Thy father thinks I loue thee for his wealth, Tho I must needs confesse at first that drew me, But since thy vertues wiped that trash away, I loue thee Nan, and so deare is it set, That whilst I liue, I nere shall thee forget. Godes pitie here comes her father.
speeches.An:: Good M. Fenton, you may assure your selfe My hart is setled vpon none but you, Tis as my father and mother please: Get their consent, you quickly shall haue mine.
But heare me speake sir. Pray misteris Page let me haue your co ̄ sent. Here nurse, theres a brace of angels to drink, Worke what thou canst for me, farwell. Yet heare me, and as I am a gentleman, Ile giue you a hundred pound toward your losse. The ̄ thus my host. Tis not vnknown to you, The feruent loue I beare to young Anne Page, And mutally her loue againe to mee: But her father still against her choise, Doth seeke to marrie her to foolish Slender, And in a robe of white this night disguised, Wherein fat Falstaffe had a mightie scare, Must Slender take her and carrie her to Catlen, And there vnknowne to any, marrie her. Now her mother still against that match, And firme for Doctor Cayus, in a robe of red By her deuice, the Doctor must steale her thence, And she hath giuen consent to goe with him. Both my good Host, to go along with me. Now here it rests, that you would procure a priest, And tarrie readie at the appointment place, To giue our harts vnited matrimonie. That hath sweet Nan and I agreed vpon, And by a robe of white, the which she weares, With ribones pendant flaring bout her head, I shalbe sure to know her, and conuey her thence, And bring her where the priest abides our co ̄ ming, And by thy furtherance there be married. So shall I euermore be bound vnto thee. Besides Ile alwaies be thy faithfull friend. Married to me, nay sir neuer storme, Tis done sir now, and cannot be vndone.
I be God that I vill, come cut and long taile, as good as any is in Glostershire, vnder the de gree of a Squire. I thanke you good misteris Anne, vncle I shall haue her. Well Nurse, if youle speake for me, Ile giue you more then Ile talke of.
Then your vndone, your but a dead man. I am glad of it, what shall we proceed any further? Content, come weele goe tell them all, And as they agree, so will we proceed. No knauery husband, it was honest mirth. Sir Iohn tis thus, your dishonest meanes To call our credits into question, Did make vs vndertake to our best, To turne your leaud lust to a merry Iest. Now M. Doctor, sonne I hope you are.
Ieshu plesse me, will you pull vp your wiues cloathes? Indeed it was good pastimes & merriments. So kad vdge me the deuises is excellent. I will also be there, and be like a Iackanapes, And pinch him most cruelly for his lecheries. Where is Pead? go you & see where Brokers sleep, And Foxe-eyed Seriants with their mase, Goe laie the Proctors in the street, And pinch the lowsie Seriants face: Spare none of these when they are a bed, But such whose nose lookes plew and red.
speeches.For,: Well send to Falstaffe, and if he come thither, Twill make vs smile and laugh one moneth togi ther.
speeches.Quic:: You Fayries that do haunt these shady groues, Looke round about the wood if you can espie A mortall that doth haunt our sacred round: If such a one you can espie, giue him his due, And leaue not till you pinch him blacke and blew: Giue them their charge Puck ere they part away.
I warrant you I will performe your will.
I smell a man of middle earth. Giue me the Tapers, I will try And if that he loue venery.
I yfaith sir come, you see your wife is wel pleased:
